patterns.usage_note: Attaches to a dictionary-form verb of perceiving or recalling (見[み]る, 聞[き]く, 思[おも]い出[だ]す) and says that every such occasion brings on the same feeling; the main clause is therefore a reaction that wells up by itself, and requests, commands, and statements of intention do not appear there. It is somewhat literary and is often doubled for sweep (見るにつけ聞くにつけ). Noun-based uses such as 何[なに]かにつけて exist and are common in speech, but the verb-attached shape is this pattern's core. Adjectives attach as well, typically in the doubled shape (嬉[うれ]しいにつけ悲[かな]しいにつけ). Compare 〜たびに, a neutral "every time" with no emotional coloring.

examples.ruby: 桜[さくら]を見[み]るにつけ、故郷[こきょう]の川[かわ]を思[おも]い出[だ]す。
examples.english: I never see cherry blossoms without thinking of the river back home.

examples.ruby: その話[はなし]を聞[き]くにつけて、胸[むね]が苦[くる]しくなる。
examples.english: Every time I hear that story, my chest tightens.

examples.ruby: 息子[むすこ]の成長[せいちょう]を感[かん]じるにつけ、時[とき]の速[はや]さに驚[おどろ]く。
examples.english: Each time I notice how my son has grown, I marvel at how fast time goes.
